title: Independence of Angola
summary: Portuguese sovereignty over Angola lapsed at midnight on 11 November 1975 without being transferred to anyone: the Alvor agreement had collapsed, and the High Commissioner left Luanda having handed power, in the formula used at the time, to the Angolan people. The MPLA, which held the capital, proclaimed the People's Republic of Angola; the FNLA and UNITA proclaimed a rival republic at Huambo. Cuban troops and a South African column were already in the country, and the civil war that followed ran, with interruptions, until 2002. Portugal recognised the MPLA government in February 1976. In the atlas it is the end of the Angolan branch of the colonial war and the clearest case of a decolonisation that handed power to nobody.
